title: A map for field observations
description: A crew saves points, photographs and notes inside a prepared area.

blocks.text: A field professional complains in a review about the limits on preparing their own maps. Gathering notes together is a possible development of that working scenario, but the quote does not confirm a request for a crew editor.

quote.text: As a wildland fire safety officer, I used to be able to download custom maps with the free version. Now, I can’t so I’m forced to purchase a plan. The wildland fire community is being pushed into using Field maps, and I may eventually go that route, too.

blocks.text: Start with preparing your own material

Find out which maps and points a crew takes with them and in what format they receive them. Test downloading and reading those with no network. Adding photographs, authorship and shared handover makes sense only after studying how observations are passed to colleagues today.

The jobs of field researchers and of firefighters can call for different maps and different working rules. One review from a professional is not enough to promise a universal tool for work in the field.
